Subject: Recap: inference cost constraints & pilot charter — next steps

Oliver — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of the things we heard and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please correct me where I got anything wrong.

Key pain points you described:
- Token/unit cost sensitivity: current run-rate on LLM features is rising fast; finance flagged ">2x" increase QoQ and wants a clear unit-economics plan.
- Latency SLAs for interactive product (95p < 350ms) with spikes during peak hours.
- Operational complexity: current infra lacks prefix caching and has limited batching support, leading to high per-request GPU usage.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Frontend -> internal inference gateway -> hosted LLM endpoints (mixed managed + self-hosted)
- Mix of Llama 2 70B for critical responses and smaller models for low-cost routes
- Request profile: heavy short-chat traffic (~3–6 tokens/user-turn + system prompts), plus occasional long-generation tasks for reports

Success criteria for the pilot (agreed candidate metrics):
- Unit cost reduction: ~35% reduction in per-1k-token cost for the chat workload (target number to be refined after sampling)
- 95th p latency maintained under 350ms for interactive flows on P95 traffic profile
- No regression in quality (sampled prompts must have parity per your internal evals)

What Redwood can deliver in the pilot (outline):
- Short-term: enable continuous batching + prefix/KV cache on the critical route, route non-critical traffic to quantized variants, and provide a dashboard of per-route token economics.
- Mid-term: test int8 quantization on a small model shard for report generation tasks to evaluate quality/cost tradeoffs.
- Ops commitment: we will instrument token-level cost breakdowns and a playbook for fallbacks if latency spikes.

Open questions / asks from Aperture to move to pilot:
1) Provide a sample 48-hour request trace (anonymized) and example prompts (we requested a CSV stub; sample-traffic-profile.csv attached).
2) Confirm which model versions you can route for the pilot (are you OK with trying a quantized variant for non-interactive routes?).
3) Decision owner & timeline: who will sign off on the pilot budget / PO?

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- This week (by Fri 7/18): Aperture uploads trace + confirms model variants.
- Next week: Redwood runs a short internal run to produce expected unit-econ delta and a risks doc.
- Week of 7/28: 2-week pilot kickoff (data sync, telemetry plumbing, smoke tests).

Attachments: redwood-inference-pilot-charter-v2.pdf (pilot charter + roles), sample-traffic-profile.csv (example trace schema).

If this looks right, I can circulate a one-page pilot SOW to your procurement and schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Tues 7/29.

Thanks — Priyom

Thanks Priyom — this is very helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 48-hour trace: we'll provide a sampled, anonymized trace by EOD Thu (7/17). Format looks good.
- Quantization: we're open to trying int8 for non-interactive report generation only for the initial pilot. Not yet comfortable moving interactive/critical flows to quantized variants without quality checks.
- Decision owner: procurement + infra lead (myself + Maria Chen) will sign off on a credit-based PO for an initial 2-week pilot (budget ceiling $15k). Maria is out this week; I can loop her in next week.

One additional constraint: we cannot reroute production traffic without a gradual canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%). We need a rollback plan and detailed telemetry before increasing traffic.

Happy to proceed on the timeline you suggested. Please include canary and rollback guidance in the pilot SOW.

Oliver
